edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.saved_converted_detail: The account, contact and deal are ready. Converting is handled on its own, so only custom fields from this save were applied; every other edit on this form was not. Reopen the lead and redo them.
edit.saved_detail: Changes to “{name}” are on the record.
edit.validation_heading: {count, plural, one {# field still needs you} other {# fields still need you}}
edit.hint_email_unique: One lead per address per org, ignoring case. The database enforces it, so a duplicate comes back as a rejected save rather than a second record.
edit.already_converted_title: This lead has already been converted
edit.already_converted_body1: Its account, contact and opportunity exist and carry the work now. The status stays where it is: reopening the lead would not remove any of them, and converting it again would build a second opportunity against the same account. The API refuses both.
edit.already_converted_body2: Everything else on this form is still editable. A converted lead is a record, not a read-only one.
edit.entering_converted_body1: An Account, a Contact and an Opportunity, with this lead's comments and attachments moved across. The lead stays as a converted record, and this is the last time you can change its status. There is no endpoint that undoes any of it.
edit.entering_converted_body2: Any other change on this form, aside from custom fields, is dropped when it saves alongside a conversion. Reopen the lead afterwards to redo it.
edit.hint_amount_placeholder: What the deal would be worth if it lands.
edit.error_last_name: A lead needs a name to be findable. First or last will do.
edit.error_email_required_convert: Converting creates a Contact, and a contact without an email cannot be reached.
edit.error_email_invalid: That does not look like an email address.
edit.error_email_taken: Another lead in this org already uses that address.
edit.error_phone_invalid: Digits and separators only. The API rejects letters, so "x123" extensions have to go in the notes.
edit.error_phone_too_long: Phone is stored in 25 characters; this is {length}.
edit.error_amount_not_number: Estimated value has to be a number.

detail.alert_needs_first_reply_text: Nobody has replied yet. A reply below is the first response. It is what stops the first-reply clock.
detail.alert_no_owner_text: Answered, but nobody owns it. Assign someone so it does not stall between people.
detail.log_description_placeholder: Traced the failed import to the CSV encoding
detail.log_time_hint: Counted back from now. To record a session from an earlier day, start and stop the timer on it.
detail.time_load_failed: The time entries could not be loaded. Nothing else on this ticket is affected.
detail.time_none_yet: No time logged yet. Start the timer, or log a session you have already worked.
detail.conversation_empty: Nothing has been said on this ticket yet. A reply below is the first response. It is what stops the first-reply clock.
detail.composer_note_hint: A note stays inside the team and does not stop the first-reply clock.

detail.error_reply_empty: Write something or attach a file before sending.
detail.error_status_stayed: Reply posted, but the status stayed put.
detail.close_result_none: Ticket closed. Nothing linked was open, so nothing else changed.

analytics.title: Service analytics
analytics.admins_only_body_prefix: Opened and closed volume, first-response attainment and the queue breakdown are whole-organisation figures, so they are limited to admins. Your own tickets are on the
analytics.stat_median_resolution_detail: Median, not mean. One three-week ticket should not move it
analytics.first_response_note: Each priority carries its own target from the escalation policy, so each one is scored against its own promise.
analytics.mix_title: What the queue is made of
analytics.mix_note: Incidents and problems are work; questions are usually a gap in the knowledge base.
analytics.mix_questions_tail: The ones that repeat belong in the knowledge base.
analytics.clock_business_hours: Elapsed time is counted inside {calendar}, so evenings, weekends and holidays do not count against a target.
analytics.clock_around_the_clock: Elapsed time is counted around the clock, no business-hours calendar is set, so evenings and weekends count against a target.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.stat_oldest_waiting_detail: A case cannot close until this clears
approvals.empty_body: Approvals land here when someone tries to close a case that a rule gates. No pending requests means no case is being held up.
approvals.own_request_note: You raised this request, so you cannot decide it yourself. Another approver must. Withdraw it if it is no longer needed.
approvals.blocked_role: This rule is cleared by {role, select, ADMIN {admins} MANAGER {managers} USER {members} other {{role}}}, and you are not one.
approvals.rule_any_role: any {role, select, ADMIN {admin} MANAGER {manager} USER {member} other {{role}}}
approvals.rules_manager_warning: One active rule is cleared by managers, but this org has only admins and members. Nobody can clear it. Name approvers on the rule, or set it to admin.
